newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Four policemen killed by gunmen in Albania.
newsitem.headline: Four policemen killed by gunmen in Albania.

text.p: Four policemen were killed in Albania overnight, three of them in the rebel-held southern town of Vlore in an apparent ambush by criminals, police said on Tuesday.
In Vlore, three policemen were chasing a suspected stolen car late on Monday night when gunmen in two other cars blocked their way and opened fire with automatic weapons, killing them instantly.
The interior ministry confirmed that another policeman was killed in the capital Tirana during the night, though it had no details of the incident.
The killings underlined calls for some sort of international force to protect a major European humanitarian effort being launched to help the stricken Balkan country.

Many towns in the south of the country, seized by rebels who rose against the previous government in anger over failed savings schemes, are effectively under the control of armed gangs, many with a criminal background.
The north of the country is under government control, but there are thousands of weapons in private hands after an orgy of looting of military depots earlier this month.

On Monday, European Union foreign ministers said they would not object to individual countries sending troops to act as military escorts for aid but for the second time in eight days shied away from organising its own multinational force to help restore order in Albania.

A policeman in Vlore, shocked by the murder of his colleagues, told Reuters on Tuesday: "If the government doesn't provide us with the security equipment we need, such as armoured cars, we will quit."
